THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Weston's Community Development Authority made a significant financial move, voting unanimously to pay off bonds tied to a now-closed tax increment district early. In Kronenwetter, the village board approved a county highway department rezoning and greenlit a fall fundraiser run at Bushka Park.

  • The Weston CDA voted unanimously to redeem its 2017A lease revenue bonds ahead of a 2031 payoff schedule, closing TIF District No. 1 after it added $354 million in assessed value since 1998.
  • Staff will bring a question about the CDA's future — including potential disbandment — to the Weston Village Board's next monthly meeting.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board approved rezoning Marathon County Highway Department property to M2 General Industrial, clearing the way for facility development.
  • Kronenwetter's board approved a 5K/3K run/walk fundraiser at Bushka Park for September 12, 2026, and directed staff to match a $5,000 parks grant.
  • Kronenwetter's CLIPP Committee is set to consider a temporary moratorium on data center development applications and a new oak wilt ordinance at its August 3 meeting.
  • The Wausau School Board is set to vote on the 2026-27 teacher salary schedule and updated employee handbook at its August 3 special meeting.

Coming up: The Wausau School Board holds a special meeting and board workshop Monday, August 3, covering teacher pay, a perceptions survey, and possible referendum discussions. Later in the week, Marathon County's Health & Human Services Committee meets Thursday, August 6, and the following Monday brings a Wausau School Board regular meeting, Weston plan and public works committees, and Kronenwetter's Police and Fire Commission.
